body.justification: The completed semialgebraic decision theorem already returns exact real-algebraic witnesses; this asks only when those feasible witnesses admit rational replacements and effective height control.
body.gap: Real-algebraic feasibility on the relevant positive exact-oracle chamber does not imply density or even existence of rational points on that chamber.
body.consumer: A positive answer would replace algebraic ambiguity witnesses by rational tables in implementations; a negative answer would confirm that the current algebraic output is sometimes necessary.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine whether every nonempty feasible separator chamber contains a rational point, and, where it does, derive an effective rational-height bound from the finite oracle and graph input.
obligation.obstruction: A semialgebraic set defined over \(\mathbb Q\) may have real-algebraic points but no rational points; neither saturation nor bounded graph structure selects a rational component of the positive exact-oracle chamber.
obligation.attempted: The earlier ideal-nonmembership route was rejected because it can witness an irrelevant real component or sign chamber. The completed algorithm instead tests the actual feasible chamber and returns an algebraic sample, but this does not rationalize that sample.
obligation.partial_result: On any rationally parameterized open chart contained in the feasible separator chamber, clearing denominators and applying the Cartesian-grid nonvanishing argument produces a rational separator after finitely many exact evaluations. The explicit four-node strictness instance supplies such a rational witness. What remains open is whether every feasible chamber relevant to a tied-family pair admits such a rational chart or point, and how to bound the resulting height.
